title: Sell Mineral Rights in Farson, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Farson, WY | Sweetwater Co
metaDescription: Farson, WY landowner on the high desert checkerboard in Sweetwater County? Get a straightforward cash offer for your mineral interest.
heroLead: Farson is high desert ranch country along the old Lander Trail, and the checkerboard survey pattern out here decides more about mineral ownership than most people realize.
intro: This part of Sweetwater County was laid out under the 1862 Union Pacific railroad land grant, odd-numbered sections going to the railroad, even sections staying federal. A century and a half later, that pattern still shapes who owns the minerals under a Farson-area ranch and who's negotiating with the BLM next door on the section over.

sections.heading: Living on checkerboard ground
paragraphs: If your family's ranch traces back to a Union Pacific land patent, you likely own both surface and minerals on your odd-numbered sections, private start to finish. If it traces back to a federal homestead patent, there's a real chance the minerals were reserved to the United States under the Stock-Raising Homestead Act, meaning you own the surface but the federal government, administered by the BLM, owns what's underneath.

sections.heading: Split estate is the rule, not the exception
paragraphs: That split between surface and mineral ownership is common enough around Farson that most ranching families here have made peace with it. It doesn't affect your right to sell whatever mineral interest you do actually hold, it just means the first step is confirming exactly what your deed covers before pricing anything.

sections.heading: What development looks like out here
paragraphs: Farson sits in high desert range with lighter oil and gas activity than the Jonah and Pinedale core to the north, but gas leasing has periodically extended this direction. Confirm your section's current lease status before assuming it's dead ground.

sections.heading: Confirming your patent type before you price anything
paragraphs: Union Pacific railroad patents and federal homestead patents look similar on the surface but carry very different mineral consequences around Farson. If your family's original patent document has survived, it will state directly whether minerals were included or reserved, saving a records trip to Green River.

faqs.question: How do I know if I own the minerals under my Farson ranch?
faqs.answer: Check whether your patent came from the Union Pacific railroad grant or a federal homestead. Stock-Raising Homestead Act patents commonly reserved minerals to the federal government, even though you own the surface.

faqs.question: Can BLM-owned minerals under my land ever be leased?
faqs.answer: Yes, federal minerals get leased through the BLM separately from your surface ownership, and you'd have no claim to those royalties unless your deed specifically includes the minerals.

faqs.question: Is there current oil and gas interest near Farson?
faqs.answer: Some, extending south from the more active Jonah and Pinedale trends in Sublette County. Check Sweetwater County Clerk records for current lease status on your section.

faqs.question: What happens if I sell a mineral interest I don't actually own?
faqs.answer: That's exactly why confirming ownership first matters. A buyer's title review would catch a federal reservation before closing, but starting with a clear answer saves everyone time and avoids a wasted conversation.
